infoSpeed Select interface present (/dev/isst_interface); intel-speed-select is not on PATH — after up, doctor reads it through the node image's pinned copy (docker exec k3d-gpu-server-0 intel-speed-select); or install it from the kernel tree (tools/power/x86/intel-speed-select)
infoSNC off (1 NUMA node per socket) on 2 compute dies (TPMI uncore domains with core agents): SNC2 makes each compute die its own NUMA node with its local memory channels (Intel Xeon 6 SNC guide 845720); up then labels k3d-gpu.io/snc=2 and replica pods get one node each
apply
BIOS (owner action): set Sub-NUMA Clustering to SNC2 (the menu name varies by board), reboot, then k3d-gpu down && k3d-gpu up
revert
BIOS: set Sub-NUMA Clustering back to Disabled, reboot
infoRDT allocation (rdt_a: cat_l2 cat_l3 cdp_l2 cdp_l3 mba) — resctrl classes are available but left off: the balloons policy ships control.rdt.enable: false because enabling it rewrites the host's /sys/fs/resctrl. To opt in, mount resctrl on the host (mount -t resctrl resctrl /sys/fs/resctrl) and set control.rdt.enable: true in nri-balloons.yml; usePodQoSAsDefaultClass then gives BestEffort/Burstable/Guaranteed pods 33%/66%/100% of the L3. To revert, set control.rdt.enable: false in nri-balloons.yml, then sudo umount /sys/fs/resctrl
infonoisy-neighbour isolation: rdt-mba — CAT + MBA can cap a neighbour's cache share and DRAM bandwidth through the RDT opt-in above (resctrl mounted: no); the shipped classes set cache shares only, so add mbAllocation: {all: ["50%"]} to the BestEffort class for bandwidth; the classes run inside the NRI balloons policy, which up deploys on hybrid or multi-NUMA hosts only
infoper socket: socket 0: DSA 3, IAA 3, QAT 3, DLB 3 (ARK default for 6741P: DSA 3, IAA 3, QAT 3, DLB 3 per socket)
infoDLB: 3 device(s) (8086:2714 DLB 2.5), no driver bound — mainline Linux has no DLB driver (Intel's out-of-tree driver or DPDK on vfio-pci) and the Kubernetes DLB device plugin was removed upstream (intel-device-plugins-for-kubernetes, 2026-09-01), so k3d-gpu exposes nothing for it
infoIntel On Demand interface present (intel_vsec.sdsi.0): on On Demand SKUs, instances above the ARK default are activated by a license (https://github.com/intel/intel-sdsi); ask the platform vendor whether activation is offered; intel_vsec.sdsi.0 state_certificate 32 B (crescent's 6741P reads 32 B with no license payload seen)
infoIn-Field Scan: intel_ifs_0 (scan) untested, image none; intel_ifs_1 (array BIST) untested — k3d-gpu never starts a test (a scan holds the core while it runs; run one on a drained core: docs.kernel.org/arch/x86/ifs.html)

CPU frequency (driver intel_pstate, mode active)

good: cores ramp to full turbo the moment a request arrives: EPP performance or balance_performance, turbo on, no frequency caps — token generation is a latency-bound loop and every ramp-up shows in time-to-first-token

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/pm/intel_pstate.html#energy-vs-performance-hints, https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/pm/cpufreq.html

why
when 1, a task waking from I/O wait gets a short min-P-state boost; it can help request handlers that block on the network or disk. Unmeasured for inference here — benchmark before keeping it

Uncore frequency (intel_uncore_frequency)

good: max_freq_khz at initial_max_freq_khz and min_freq_khz at initial_min_freq_khz: the hardware (UFS, or ELC on TPMI parts) picks the uncore clock inside the full range. A floor pinned high for decode is unproven (EXPERIMENTS.md H29, INCONCLUSIVE), so it is not suggested

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/pm/intel_uncore_frequency_scaling.html

DRAM speed, bandwidth and ECC

good: modules at the platform's plan-of-record (POR) speed for how the slots are populated; single-stream CPU and iGPU decode is bound by DRAM bandwidth. Memory errors counted by an EDAC driver

sources: SMBIOS DSP0134 7.18 (type 17, as dmidecode.c decodes it), Intel datasheet 743844 rev. 015 table 25 (13th/14th Gen Core DDR support matrix, https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/743844), https://docs.kernel.org/driver-api/edac.html

https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/products/sku/241828/intel-xeon-6741p-processor-288m-cache-2-50-ghz/specifications.html

noteECC modules, but no EDAC memory controller is registered: corrected and uncorrected errors are not counted (dram.ecc=unmonitored)

/sys/devices/system/edac/mc/ (no mc*), /sys/firmware/dmi/entries/17-*/raw
why
without an EDAC driver a failing module shows up only as crashes or silent corruption; with one, ce_count/ue_count give early warning

revert

Isolation for sandboxed agents

good: /dev/kvm usable for microVM sandboxes, each GPU alone in its IOMMU group, split-lock detection on, CET known, GPU observation streams limited to CAP_PERFMON

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/driver-api/vfio.html (IOMMU groups), https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.html (split_lock_detect), https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/sysctl/kernel.html (split_lock_mitigate), kernel source drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_perf.c and drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_observation.c (paranoid sysctls), Intel SDM vol. 4 335592-093 (IA32_S_CET 6A2H, IA32_TME_ACTIVATE 982H)
